summary: This program asks for a Celsius temperature, keeps re-prompting until the reader types a valid number within range, then converts it to Fahrenheit. A finally block prints a closing message whether the conversion succeeds or an unexpected error interrupts it.

lines.text: Using print instead of println leaves the cursor on the same line, so the reader's typing appears right after the prompt.
This is a try-with-resources statement: the Scanner declared in the parentheses is closed automatically when the block ends, no matter how it ends.
The capital-D Double wrapper type is used here because it can hold null, which marks "no valid temperature collected yet"; a plain double cannot.
A deliberately infinite loop that keeps asking for input; the only way out is the break once a good value arrives.
Reading the whole line and trimming it removes stray spaces so that " 25 " still parses as a number.
An inner try handles just the parsing failure, leaving the outer try free to catch anything else that goes wrong.
This converts the text into a number, and throws NumberFormatException when the text is not numeric.
The value parsed correctly but falls outside the accepted range, which is a validation problem rather than an exception.
continue jumps back to the top of the while loop to ask again, skipping the code that would accept the value.
The value has passed both checks, so it is stored in the variable that lives outside the loop.
break is the single exit from the infinite loop, taken only once a valid temperature has been captured.
Catching only NumberFormatException keeps the recovery narrow: bad text is expected and handled, while real bugs are not swallowed here.
The Double object is unwrapped to a plain double automatically here, a conversion Java calls unboxing.
A broad safety net for anything unforeseen, such as the input stream ending before a valid number is entered.
The finally block runs after the try or the catch, on success and on failure alike, which makes it the right place for cleanup or a closing message.
Pulling the formula into its own method keeps the conversion separate from all the input-handling code.
Because celsius is a double, celsius * 9 is a double and the division by 5 keeps its fractional part.
